summary: Ferry County, WA summit cupola cabin; build year disputed (1919/1922/1923); removed 1950; FFLOS-registered 2012; WTA describes lookout remains at the summit.

facts.status_note: Cupola cabin removed in 1950 (firelookout.com says destroyed); WTA describes remains of an old fire lookout at the southern end of the summit

staffing.status: Lookout staffing recorded for 1923, 1928, 1929, 1944 and 1945; no later staffing given

access.note: Summit reached by a hiking route described by WTA; the page gives no closure or permit rules. Level inferred from the route description, so confirm with the Forest Service

visit.trail_note: Reached from the Kettle Crest route by a spur trail; WTA describes the round trip as 28 miles

events.note: Completed by July 1, 1923 per a September 1923 report. Register gives 1919, firelookout.com 1922, and a register photo caption says under construction 1922
Used as a lookout for the first time in 1923; H.P. Hasler is listed as lookout personnel that year
S.B. Hayward listed as lookout personnel
Mr. and Mrs. Chas. Bouk of Republic were the lookout
Homer Therleen listed as lookout personnel
Cupola cabin removed; firelookout.com says destroyed
Registered November 23, 2012; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says 1919, firelookout.com says 1922, and a register photo caption says under construction 1922. Only the September 1923 report describes completion, so 1923 is recorded as the year it was finished. The 1919 and 1922 dates are not explained by any source read.
Register and Willhite say the cabin was removed in 1950; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1950. Recorded as removed, with the destroyed wording noted.

sources.title: White Mountain via Kettle Crest Trail South

notes_for_editor: Build year is disputed: 1919 (register), 1922 (firelookout.com and register photo caption), 1923 (completion report); the story says so. Brief said access unknown; access is now recorded as public from the WTA route description only, so confirm. Staffing names come from firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb and are not a full list. A line about cement steps in the WTA text belongs to the Barnaby Buttes side trip, not White Mountain, and was not used. No fire history found in the sources read. Search results mentioned a 1988 White Mountain Fire; not used. WillhiteWeb 1923 newspaper quotes contain garbled characters, so the quotes used avoid them.
